title: Baba Ganoush
subtitle: Charred aubergine dip with tahini and lemon
excerpt: Whole aubergines are charred directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill until completely collapsed, then blended with tahini, garlic, and lemon. The smoky flavour comes entirely from the charring process.
sourceNotes: Baba ganoush is a Levantine dish eaten across Lebanon, Syria, and Israel. The name translates roughly as spoiled father in Arabic, though the etymology is disputed. The dish appears in cookbooks across the region from the 19th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. The flavour deepens in the fridge.

content.text: The aubergines must be completely blackened and collapsed before you remove them from the heat. Undercharring is the most common mistake. If using a grill, keep them as close to the element as possible and turn them regularly.
If using a gas hob, place the aubergines directly over the flame. Turn every 5 minutes using tongs.
If using a grill, place the aubergines on a baking tray under a very hot grill. Turn every 8 minutes.
Cook for 35 to 40 minutes total, until the skin is completely charred and the aubergines feel very soft when pressed.
Transfer to a colander over a bowl. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Peel away and discard the charred skin. The flesh inside should be very soft and smoky.
Let the flesh drain in the colander for 5 minutes to remove any bitter liquid.
Put the flesh in a blender with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, and cumin.
Blend briefly. The texture should be slightly rough, not completely smooth.
Taste and season with salt. Add more lemon juice if needed.
Spread onto a plate. Drizzle with olive oil and scatter over the parsley.

items.cause: The aubergines were not charred fully on the outside.
items.fix: Push charring further until the skin is completely blackened.

items.cause: The aubergine flesh was not drained after peeling.
items.fix: Always drain in a colander for at least 5 minutes before blending.
